StageStage 2, Accept the order, as a whole
EntersSubmitted
LeavesPaid, or Cancelled
Expected by the customer who placed the orderthe order is accepted when the shopper expects, and not lost to a payment outage (proposed)
Stepeach step of Stage 2, Accept the order
1The order is released for stock checking when the grace period endsRight outcome: AwaitingValidation within 1.5 minutes of "OrderDate", with its OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidation outbox row at State 2 (proposed)
2Stock is confirmed for every item of the orderRight outcome: StockConfirmed only when every ordered product is in the catalogue with AvailableStock of at least its units; Description 'All the items were confirmed with available stock.' (proposed)
3The order is cancelled because an item is out of stockRight outcome: Cancelled, with Description naming the products without stock (proposed)
4Payment is taken for the orderRight outcome: Paid, with the order total taken once from the buyer's payment method (proposed)
5The order is cancelled because payment failedRight outcome: Cancelled, with no payment taken (proposed)
6The order is cancelled at the customer's requestRight outcome: Cancelled before any payment is taken (proposed)

The flow’s 5 alerts, each placed once: at the level it watches, and in the health layer of the measure it is built on (business, application or technology; a business alert is marked impact when it counts cases that failed what was expected of them, and health when it counts whether the work is happening). The kit proposes alerts only on what happens to the flow’s cases, and leaves service and store signals to the runbooks, so empty Application and Technology columns are how the kit works, not a gap in this run. The threshold, the window and whether it pages someone are set by the people who run it, not by the kit.
